subject.title: Concurrency: NodeConnector.ForwardIfCurrent invokes subscriber delegates while holding _clientLifecycleLock (lifecycle stall/reentrancy hazard)

question: Should `NodeConnector` retain its documented synchronous-under-lock subscriber contract, or should maintainers sponsor a retirement-safe out-of-lock dispatch design that prevents lifecycle stalls?
rationale: Both choices intentionally define the connection event contract: a naive lock removal breaks the stated retired-client ordering guarantee, while retaining the lock preserves a known blocking and reentrancy hazard.

options.title: Sponsor retirement-safe dispatch
options.body: Introduce a bounded per-generation dispatch/completion barrier with deterministic tests proving lifecycle progress and no post-retirement publication.

options.title: Accept synchronous callback contract
options.body: Keep validation and subscriber invocation atomic under the lifecycle lock, explicitly document the nonblocking/non-reentrant subscriber requirement, and close this as accepted by design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor retirement-safe dispatch
recommendation.body: Introduce a bounded per-generation dispatch/completion barrier with deterministic tests proving lifecycle progress and no post-retirement publication.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context identifies this contributor as the only person who has traced and documented both sides of the dispatch-contract tradeoff; confidence is limited because current-main ownership history was unavailable in the review packet.
